release_notes:
## Fixes
- The version next to the title now shows the real, full version instead of being stuck at v1.0. It was never a display problem: when the app couldn't read its own version.json it substituted the string "1.0", which looks exactly like a real version
- The "update available" bar no longer keeps coming back after you have already updated. That same substituted "1.0" was being compared against every release, so it was always older and the banner could never be satisfied — reinstalling the update it was asking for changed nothing
- version.json is now looked for in three places (next to the app, inside the bundle's Resources, and in Application Support), and every update writes a copy to Application Support, which survives both a rebuild and a bundle that isn't writable. An update that can't record its own version now fails loudly instead of quietly leaving the app unable to tell what it is running
- About now shows which version.json the number came from, so a wrong version can be diagnosed from the menu instead of by digging through the app bundle

## Also in this build
- Social Media exports find the Watermark track whatever the clip is named (shipped in 1.0.8)
- Mute Master Clips no longer mutes more tracks than intended (shipped in 1.0.8)
- Mute Master Clips failing to mute at all is still NOT fixed. The nest log reports every video track's real mute state at three points — after the un-mute/target step, after the mute step, and on the first nested episode. One nest run with the box checked, and those three lines, is what's needed to fix it
